records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The catch-block prisma.workflowReminder.update is itself unguarded — if the original error was a database/Prisma failure, the compensating update throws inside the catch, crashing the loop before console.log and skipping the remaining unscheduled reminders in the same batch. A transient DB outage during one reminder's send leaves the loop aborted mid-batch: subsequent reminders in this run are never attempted and their retryCount is never recorded, so they lose a retry attempt they were entitled to.
records.rationale: The diff adds an `await prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)` inside the `catch (error)` block (and also in the `else` branch) without guarding it. If the original failure was due to Prisma/DB outage, this compensating `update` can throw as well, which would escape the catch and abort the loop/handler before `console.log(...)`, preventing subsequent `unscheduledReminders` from being processed in this batch.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The new OR clause deletes WorkflowReminder rows of every method, not just SMS, whenever retryCount > 1. A failed EMAIL (or other-method) reminder that was retried twice is permanently deleted by this SMS-scheduling endpoint, so the email reminder silently disappears and is never sent — cross-feature data destruction caused by the retryCount tracking being scoped to the wrong model-wide query instead of being constrained to method: SMS.
records.rationale: In `scheduleSMSReminders.ts`, the `deleteMany` filter was changed to `where: { OR: [ { method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, scheduledDate: { lte: ... } }, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } } ] }`. The second OR branch (`retryCount > 1`) has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` constraint, so it will delete *any* `WorkflowReminder` row (regardless of method) once `retryCount` exceeds 1. Since `retryCount` is added to the shared `WorkflowReminder` model (`schema.prisma` + migration), this can cause non-SMS reminders to be deleted by this SMS endpoint.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The new `OR: [{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }]` branch drops both the `method: SMS` filter and the `scheduledDate lte now` guard from the deleteMany, so any WorkflowReminder row with retryCount > 1 is deleted regardless of method or scheduled date. A reminder that failed scheduling twice (retryCount=2) and then succeeds on the third pass gets a Twilio referenceId created, but the next cron run deletes its WorkflowReminder row via the retryCount clause — the Twilio scheduled SMS still fires with no DB record left to cancel or reschedule (the existing deleteMany was the cancellation cleanup path). Symmetrically, a future-dated reminder that is still actively being retried is deleted mid-retry-cycle instead of only past-due ones, so it never gets its remaining attempts. If any other code path (email reminders, future features) ever writes retryCount, those non-SMS rows are also hard-deleted by this query since the method filter no longer applies to the whole query.

records.issue_text: [BUG] retryCount is incremented via read-modify-write using the value selected at the top of the run (`reminder.retryCount + 1`) rather than an atomic `retryCount: { increment: 1 }`. Two overlapping invocations of this endpoint/cron (or a retry racing the cron) both read retryCount=0 and both write 1, under-counting retries so the >1 cleanup cap allows more send attempts than designed, and in general the cap is enforced against a value that can lose updates. Prisma's `increment` operator makes the lost update mechanically avoidable.
records.rationale: The diff shows retryCount being incremented using a read-modify-write pattern based on the previously selected value: `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` (added in both the `else` branch after attempting to schedule and in the `catch`). Since `reminder.retryCount` is read earlier via `findMany(... select: { ...select, retryCount: true })`, concurrent invocations can both read the same value (e.g., 0) and both write 1, losing an update. This can under-count retries and affect logic that relies on `retryCount` (e.g., the new deleteMany condition `retryCount: { gt: 1 }`). Prisma supports atomic

records.issue_text: [BUG] The deleteMany expansion silently rewrites the endpoint's objective from 'clean up past-due SMS reminders' to 'destroy any reminder with retryCount > 1, regardless of method or scheduled date'. Because retryCount lives on the shared WorkflowReminder model and the OR branch drops the method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter entirely, any reminder row (including email/other-method reminders, if this field is ever incremented elsewhere) with retryCount > 1 is permanently deleted; more immediately, an SMS reminder whose scheduledDate is still in the future but which failed scheduling twice is hard-deleted on the next run, so a customer's upcoming reminder silently disappears with no audit trail — a data-loss failure the original intent (cleanup of already-past reminders) never authorized. Counter-rebuttal: 'this is the intended retry cap' — but a cap on retries that manifests as deletion of the reminder row itself (rather than marking it cancelled/exhausted) changes the deletion semantics of this cleanup query without that being the stated objective of the change.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The deleteMany OR clause deletes reminders with retryCount > 1 regardless of method or scheduledDate, wiping reminders that are not SMS and not past-due. When the Twilio send fails twice (network error, Twilio outage, or a bad 'to' number) the reminder row is hard-deleted after the second failure, so any Email or other-method reminder sharing that row — and any still-future scheduled SMS reminder that hit two transient errors — is silently destroyed and never delivered or retryable; users miss mandatory reminders (e.g. booking confirmations) with no audit trail since rows are deleted rather than marked failed.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] retryCount increments both in the else branch and in the catch block, so any error thrown before the send (e.g. in Twilio client setup or the to/from payload construction) still counts as a retry and drives the reminder toward deletion. An operator with a misconfigured Twilio env var or a recurring exception in reminder processing loses all pending reminders across every workflow after two cron runs (deleteMany then removes them), converting a transient infra misconfiguration into permanent data loss; the catch path increments even when no SMS was attempted.
records.rationale: The diff makes retryCount drive deletion and increments it on any failure, even if no SMS was actually sent. At the start, `deleteMany` now deletes any `WorkflowReminder` with `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` (no method/date filter) via the added `OR` clause. Later, `retryCount` is incremented both when `scheduledSMS.sid` is falsy (`else { ... retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 }`) and on any exception in the `catch` block (same update). An SMS reminder whose Twilio scheduling errors twice has its row hard-deleted; the booking attendee never gets the reminder and there is no residual record that it was attempted or failed — operators cannot audit or retry it, and the deletion is irreversible.

Any future or concurrent writer that increments retryCount on a non-SMS (e.g. email/cal) WorkflowReminder causes this handler to delete those reminders too, even though this endpoint's contract is to clean up only past-due SMS reminders.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The retryCount increment is a read-then-write (data: { retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 }) rather than an atomic increment, and it runs before the deleteMany's retryCount>1 cutoff takes effect on the next invocation — the whole gate is a per-cron-cycle race. If two overlapping cron invocations of this handler fetch the same reminder before either increments, both schedule a Twilio message (duplicate SMS) and the count only advances to 1, deferring the retry cap by a full cycle; attendees get duplicate texts during any handler overlap.

Two overlapping runs of the schedule endpoint (cron overlap or manual + cron) both read retryCount=0 and both write 1, so a reminder that failed twice across overlapping runs is treated as having failed once and gets an extra retry — or conversely the retry cap is enforced inconsistently; also the endpoint has no in-flight lock, so both runs schedule the SMS and the attendee gets duplicate messages.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The catch block performs an awaited prisma update with no guard, so a database failure inside the error handler escapes the try/catch and aborts the loop mid-batch. If the update inside catch throws (e.g. the reminder was concurrently deleted so the unique-where fails with P2025, or a transient DB error), the exception propagates out of the for-loop, the handler returns a 500 after some reminders were already scheduled, and the remaining reminders in the batch are neither scheduled nor retried — the original error is also replaced by the prisma error, losing it.
records.rationale: The diff adds an `await prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)` inside the `catch (error)` block (and also in the `else` branch) without guarding it. If the original failure was due to Prisma/DB outage, this compensating `update` can throw as well, which would escape the catch and abort the loop/handler before `console.log(...)`, preventing subsequent `unscheduledReminders` from being processed in this batch.
